text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VJESNIK

- President Tudjman and UN Transitional Administrator Klein held talks on completing the peaceful reintegration of Eastern Slavonia and agree for local authorities to be established within 30 days of the April elections and for the area to remain demilitarised.
- Croatia and Switzerland to sign a document on the scrapping of visas on May 13.
- Croatia to start negotiations on customs concessions for goods and services with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) on May 15 and 16 in Geneva.
- March jobless figures up 0.2 percent to 284,611 in comparison to February.
VECERNJI LIST
- Changes in the health system: Hospitals are to be awarded a monthly ration of medicines as producers are still owed money for 700 million kuna worth of medicines.

- The first round of talks between the Zagreb city assembly opposition parties ends. The Croatian Peasant Party's three deputies, who have the balance of power in the assembly, have yet to decide who they will join a coalition with.
- Feral Tribune journalists Viktor Ivancic and Marinko Culic are to be re-tried for insulting the president after their previous acquittal was annulled.
- Croatia and foreign trade partners: The brokering of agreements on free trade zones opens up the possibility of increased exports to Macedonia, Slovenia, Poland and Asia.
- The registraton of voucher users will begin at the end of May, says assistant Privatisation Minister Damir Ostovic in an interview.

- A sharp increase in retail sales comes as a result of customer loans being offered since the start of 1997. January 1997 retail sales were 2.6 billion kuna, up by 630 million kuna compared to January 1996.
- David Bowie to hold a concert in Zagreb on July 1.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA
- British insurance brokerage Willis Faber & Dumas plans to win a larger share of the Croatian market through local partner Helios, says its nautical department director Richard Close-Smith.
- Croatia Airlines' direct twice-weekly flights between London and Split on the coast expected to boost the number of British visitors to Dalmatia.
- Economic commentary: Croatia must enforce the discipline imposed by the IMF so as not to thwart its support, which is the key to further development.
- Privredna Banka Zagreb recovers under the government's rehabilitation programme, launched in December 1996.
- Stock market: Levi's decision to extend a manufacturing license to Varteks propels its shares up. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
